drafted_from: tool:list-what-a-character-says's row in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/ and the tests in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "List every caption line the parrot says in my episodes, from the turns files, into a table I can quote." It runs tool:list-what-a-character-says and writes character-lines.tsv.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one settings row of yours (record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) or the settings you pass, and works on files in the show's folder.
instructions: 1. Make the show's folder and the YouTube library folder the run may change, and have the catalog.tsv (tool:catalog-a-channels-videos-by-format), voice/<id>.turns.json (tool:find-when-a-character-speaks) and the captions in the folders. Put the keys the row needs (none: it reads no settings key) in your settings row or pass them as settings.

2. Say the sentence in start_here to your AI. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:list-what-a-character-says and the input in the worked example; the door asks for the granted folder.
3. Read the last line it prints, {"result": ...}, or {"error": ...} saying what to fix (a missing settings key is named).
4. Quote lines from character-lines.tsv; they are YouTube's auto-captions, so the spelling is YouTube's.

worked_examples.title: Two caption lines inside one turn
worked_examples.given: From the sample run in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json and LinesTest in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/test_measures.py: vid-a has one turn from 10.0 to 14.0 s and captions "the keeper speaks" (5 s for 4 s), ">> crackers please" (9 s for 2 s) and "and a storm" (11.5 s for 2 s).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"table": "{grant:change-a-folder}/show/character-lines.tsv", "lines": 2}}; the table rows are vid-a 20300105 episode second 9 turn 10.0-14.0 ">> crackers please" and second 11 "and a storm"; "the keeper speaks" is left out because less than half of it lies in the turn.
